criteria.text: Diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease; treatment initiated at mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia stage
Patient is 50 years of age or older
Prescribed by or in consultation with a neurologist
Beta-amyloid plaques verified by PET scan or CSF testing
Documented brain MRI within the last year showing no localized superficial siderosis, fewer than 10 brain microhemorrhages, and no brain hemorrhages greater than 1 cm in the past year
Objective evidence of cognitive impairment at screening
Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) global score of 0.5
Mini-Mental State Exam (MMSE) score of at least 24
Other known causes of dementia ruled out (including vascular dementia and Parkinson's disease dementia)
Not taking blood thinners other than aspirin 81 mg or less
No brain hemorrhage, bleeding disorder, or cerebrovascular abnormalities in the last 6 months
No significant systemic illness or infection in the past 30 days
No unstable angina, myocardial infarction, advanced chronic heart failure, or clinically significant conduction abnormalities within 1 year prior to screening

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Aduhelm (aducanumab-avwa), an amyloid beta-directed antibody, Criteria Version 1: Original 7/16/2021; Approval 9/17/21; Effective 11/1/21. The effective_date remains 2021-11-01.

Encoded: approval criteria 1-9, with the closed Alzheimer's disease indication restricted to initiation at mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia stage per the PDF FDA indications; denial criteria 2-5 are approval-blocking predicates. Denial criterion 1 is failure to meet approval criteria.

Initial approval: up to 3 months. Reauthorization: up to 6 months if MRI obtained prior to the 7th and 12th doses shows no increase in size or number of ARIA-H, and documented evidence shows positive response, slowed rate of cognitive decline, and no adverse reactions. These reauthorization requirements are notes only, not fully predicated.

ARIA caution: enhanced clinical vigilance during the first 8 doses, particularly titration. Symptoms suggestive of ARIA require clinical evaluation, including MRI testing if indicated. ARIA imaging schedule and monitoring are not fully predicated; this pack remains partial.

PDL context only: Aduhelm is non-preferred in ALZHEIMER'S AGENTS. Leqembi is a same-class anti-amyloid alternative, subject to its own criteria and separate evaluation. Kisunla is also a same-class anti-amyloid alternative, subject to its own criteria and separate evaluation. Preferred oral Alzheimer's agents such as donepezil are PDL context only; no oral step-therapy requirement is encoded.

criteria.text: Acute intermittent treatment of hypomobility/off episodes in Parkinson’s disease (approval criterion 2 and FDA indications).

notes: Partial encoding from AK Apokyn/Kynmobi (apomorphine) Criteria Version 1. Original: 10/07/20; Approval: 11/20/20. PDF Effective is printed as 1/11//20 (malformed; commonly rendered 1/11/20). effective_date uses the unambiguous approval date 2020-11-20 rather than the archived stub date 2026-03-01; the source extraction is retained unchanged.

Apokyn injectable is indicated for acute intermittent hypomobility/off episodes associated with advanced Parkinson’s disease; Kynmobi sublingual films are indicated for acute intermittent off episodes in Parkinson’s disease. Approval criteria 1–5 and the concurrent 5-HT3 antagonist denial are encoded. Failure to meet approval criteria is also a denial.
Duration (notes only): Initial Approval up to 3 months; Reauthorization Approval up to 12 months.

Quantity limits (notes only): Apokyn — 5 injections per day / 150 injections per month; Kynmobi — 5 films per day / 150 films per month. Duration and quantity enforcement require manual review; this pack remains partial.

Cautions (notes only): Concomitant antihypertensive medications and vasodilators may increase risk of hypotension, myocardial infarction, falls and injuries. Syncope and hypotension/orthostatic hypotension may occur; monitor blood pressure.

Cautions (notes only): Withdrawal-emergent hyperpyrexia and confusion may occur with rapid dose reduction or withdrawal. May prolong QTc and cause torsades de pointes or sudden death; consider risk factors prior to initiation. Dopamine antagonists may diminish apomorphine effectiveness. Patients 65 years and older were more likely to experience certain adverse events in clinical trials.

The FDA summary describes lupus nephritis in adults; the pediatric IV path follows the explicit Alaska approval criteria. Standard therapy or contraindication is separately attested for each indication.
Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 4 months; reauthorization up to 12 months if the prescriber documents disease improvement.

Quantity and dosing (manual review): IV 120 mg or 400 mg vials, 10 mg/kg at weeks 0, 2, 4 then every 4 weeks. Subcutaneous 200 mg/ml prefilled autoinjector/syringe for active lupus nephritis: 8 injections in the first 28 days, then 4 injections per 28 days. HCPCS: J0490.

Cautions (notes only): use caution with severe or chronic infections; serious and sometimes fatal infections have occurred. Evaluate new or worsening neurological signs and symptoms for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). Consider premedication for infusion and hypersensitivity reactions. Assess depression and suicidality before treatment and monitor during treatment.

FDA limitations: efficacy has not been evaluated in severe active CNS lupus; not studied with other biologics and use is not recommended in these situations. Subcutaneous dosing has not been evaluated and is not approved below age 18 in this source.
PDL status unknown: source is silent. Therapeutic class retains the stub value other. Lupkynis is linked as an LN peer requiring separate eligibility evaluation, not concomitant use.
Remaining gaps: duration, reauthorization disease-improvement documentation, weight-based dosing, quantity enforcement and cautions require manual review.

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Berinert Criteria Version 1; Last updated 1/7/2013; Approved 01/18/2013. The effective_date 2022-11-01 is retained from the archived stub and is not the PDF approval date.
Indicated for acute abdominal, facial, or laryngeal HAE attacks in adults and adolescents. The PDF supplies no numeric age cutoff; age eligibility requires manual review.
A letter of medical necessity and all necessary documentation substantiating every approval criterion are required; document verification remains manual review.
ER documentation is required to substantiate monthly abdominal or respiratory attacks requiring hospital ER intervention in the previous 6 months.

Both preventative medication classes must have an insufficient response or contraindication: 17α-alkylated androgens (danazol, stanozolol, oxandrolone, methyltestosterone) AND antifibrinolytic agents (aminocaproic acid, tranexamic acid). Any androgen contraindication must be documented by an endocrinologist; verify documentation manually.
The safety and efficacy of Berinert for prophylactic therapy have not been established. Prophylaxis is excluded by the closed indication.
PDL context: pdl_20260601_text.txt lists BERINERT (IV) as non-preferred (OFF) in HAE TREATMENTS, effective 6/1/2026.
Ekterly is an acute HAE treatment alternative requiring separate evaluation under its own criteria.
Firazyr is an adult acute HAE treatment alternative requiring separate evaluation under its own indication and criteria.

Approval Criteria column controls encoded ages: severe axillary hyperhidrosis age ≥17, despite age ≥18 in the page 1 FDA indication matrix. Page 1 matrix and individual FDA labeling remain manual review; neurogenic detrusor overactivity approval age is ≥5.
Notes only — FDA-recommended doses and maximum cumulative doses require manual review. Cumulative Botox must not exceed 400 units in 3 months from all procedures.
Maximum quantities (notes only): OAB Botox 100 units/12 weeks; neurogenic bladder Botox 200 units/12 weeks; chronic migraine Botox 155 units/12 weeks.

Spasticity quantities (notes only): Botox 400 units/12 weeks; Dysport pediatric lesser of 30 units/kg or 1000 units/12 weeks, adult 1500 units/12 weeks. Xeomin upper limb 400 units total divided among affected muscles, pediatric maximum 200 units per upper limb.

Cervical dystonia quantities (notes only): Botox 400 units/3 months (12 weeks); Dysport initial 500 units/12 weeks, subsequent increase no more than 250 units above previous dose up to 1000 units/12 weeks; Myobloc 5000 units/12 weeks or 10000 units/16 weeks; Xeomin 120 units/12 weeks.
Hyperhidrosis Botox maximum 50 units per axilla/12 weeks. Strabismus Botox maximum 25 units for any one muscle/12 weeks; subsequent dose no more than twice previous dose or 25 units. Notes only.

Blepharospasm quantities (notes only): Botox 200 cumulative units/30 days and 400 units/12 weeks; Xeomin 35 units per eye/12 weeks. Chronic sialorrhea: Myobloc 3500 units/12 weeks; Xeomin adult 100 units/12 weeks, pediatric 75 units/16 weeks.
Renewal migraine response (notes only): headache frequency decreased by ≥2 headache days from baseline in previous month; denial column applies beyond second treatment.
Length of authorization up to 6 months. Reauthorization requires documented clinical response and progress and absence of limiting adverse effects. Notes only.

Non-FDA approved medical, non-cosmetic indications require case-by-case review using current CMS LCD L38809, supporting literature demonstrating safety/efficacy in representative population, medical necessity letter with prior therapies, and maximally specific ICD codes. These requests are outside the closed automated indication paths; cosmetic use is denied.

Black Box Warning (notes only): distant spread of toxin effect, hours to weeks after injection, can cause generalized weakness, diplopia, ptosis, dysphagia, dysphonia, dysarthria, urinary incontinence and breathing difficulties. Swallowing/breathing difficulties can be life-threatening or fatal; greatest risk likely in children treated for spasticity, also adults and predisposed patients, at approved or unapproved uses and comparable or lower doses.
Evidence verification, FDA indication matrix, dosing, maximum quantities, cumulative doses, renewal, duration and warnings remain manual review. No alternatives encoded.

BASD due to a single enzyme defect confirmed by abnormal urinary bile acid on Fast Atom Bombardment ionization–Mass Spectrometry (FAB-MS) analysis OR molecular genetic testing consistent with the diagnosis (approval criterion 2).
Patient exhibits liver disease, steatorrhea, or complications due to reduced fat-soluble vitamin absorption (approval criterion 3a).
Cholbam will be used as adjunctive therapy (approval criterion 3b).
Baseline liver function labs documented: AST, ALT, GGT, ALP, bilirubin, INR (final approval criterion, numbered 3 in source).
No complete biliary obstruction develops (denial criterion 2).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Cholbam (cholic acid) Criteria Version 1: Original 12/19/2022; Approval 01/20/2023; Effective 03/01/2023.

Encoded: two closed FDA indication paths, specialist requirement, indication-gated BASD confirmation or peroxisomal manifestations and adjunctive therapy, baseline liver labs, and absence of complete biliary obstruction. Failure to meet approval criteria is represented by these clauses. No numeric age gate is stated.
Specialty consultation values are accepted per the requested encoding convention; the source wording is prescribed by a specialist gastroenterologist or hepatologist.

Monitoring (notes only): AST, ALT, GGT, alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin and INR every month for the first 3 months, every 3 months for the next 9 months, every 6 months during the next three years and annually thereafter. Administer the lowest dose that effectively maintains liver function.
Duration (notes only): initial approval 3 months; reauthorization 12 months with chart notes documenting improvements in liver function labs. Updated labs are required for renewal.
Quantity (notes only): 10–15 mg/kg/day administered in one to two doses daily; concomitant familial hypertriglyceridemia may require 11–17 mg/kg/day, adjusted based on clinical response.
Documentation verification, monitoring, lowest effective dose, duration, renewal response and quantity require manual review; this pack remains partial. No alternatives are specified.

criteria.text: Routine prophylaxis against HAE attacks in adolescent and adult patients.
Documented diagnosis of hereditary angioedema (HAE) by an immunologist (approval criterion 1).
History consistent with monthly abdominal or respiratory HAE attacks requiring hospital ER intervention in the previous 6 months, generally with usage of Berinert or Kalbitor (approval criterion 2).
Patient is NOT concurrently taking an ACE inhibitor or estrogen replacement therapy (approval criterion 3).
Insufficient response or contraindication to BOTH 17α-alkylated androgens AND antifibrinolytic agents (approval criterion 4).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Cinryze Criteria Version 1; Last updated 7/6/2011. The effective_date uses this last-updated date; the PDF approval date is an unfilled placeholder (xx/xx/xxxx).

Indicated for routine prophylaxis against HAE attacks in adolescent and adult patients. The PDF supplies no numeric age cutoff; age eligibility requires manual review. Acute treatment is excluded by the closed indication.
A letter of medical necessity and all necessary documentation substantiating every approval criterion are required; document verification remains manual review.

ER documentation is required to substantiate monthly abdominal or respiratory attacks requiring hospital ER intervention in the previous 6 months, generally with usage of Berinert or Kalbitor. Medication usage is context, not a separate mandatory therapy step.

Both preventative medication classes must have an insufficient response or contraindication: 17α-alkylated androgens (danazol, stanozolol, oxandrolone, methyltestosterone) AND antifibrinolytic agents (aminocaproic acid, tranexamic acid). Any androgen contraindication must be documented by an endocrinologist; verify documentation manually.
The Alaska Medicaid Medical Director will work with hospital emergency departments to ensure the availability of Berinert or Kalbitor for acute attacks of HAE for authorized recipients.
Andembry and Dawnzera are prophylaxis peers; Berinert treats acute HAE attacks. Each linked peer requires separate evaluation under its own indication and criteria.

Submitted treatment plan defines prophylactic and on-demand regimens, infusion intervals, and number of doses to be dispensed per fill.

notes: Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid Hemophilia Factor Program: Version 1; Approved 11/17/17; PDF Effective 5/1/2019. The stub effective_date 2017-01-01 is preserved; appendix footers still say Effective pending.

Encoded: only the five Criteria for Approval bullets: closed diagnosis list, regional HTC affiliation, enrolled prescribing/dispensing provider SOC agreement, defined prophylactic and on-demand treatment plan including infusion intervals and doses per fill, and continued infusion logging. No age, severity, inhibitor-status, specialty, or prior-therapy gates are added.

Authorizations (notes only): initial up to 3 months; reauthorization may be longer with required clinical documentation and established clinical stability. Authorizations are patient/prescriber/pharmacy-specific; changes require formal transfer. Emergency one-time transfer overrides may be requested through the Clinical Call Center if delay could adversely affect patient health.

Quantity (notes only): based on treatment plan, no more than one month supply; prophylactic and on-demand product must not be combined in the same claim; dispensing tolerance ±5%. max_units is null; quantity enforcement requires manual review.

Provider/Facility Adherence and Required Documentation (notes only): all program requirements apply to enrolled providers. Prescriber-signed intake/treatment plan and new-patient, annual, and changed-information review include identifiers/contact information, demographics, height/weight, diagnosis/confirmation, baseline and on-regimen factor levels, severity, venous access, inhibitor status/date, allergies, both dosing regimens, prescriber and HTC. Individual intake items are not approval predicates.

Provider operations (notes only): regional/home HTC coordination, prescriber product selection and treatment responsibility, annual pharmacy notice by July 1, 24/7 pharmacist and emergency access, nursing access, home assessment, storage, inventory, waste disposal, education and communication/delivery needs. Pharmacy maintains infusion logs, reviews compliance/utilization variances, and supplies logs to the State on request.

Dispensing/delivery SOC (notes only): patient pharmacy choice and patient/caregiver-initiated fills, no auto fills, documented shipment authorization and stock on hand, one-month supply minus stock with five-day emergency supply allowance. Established-patient delivery within two days, new nonemergency delivery within three days, active-bleed delivery within 24 hours; cold chain, physical recipient signature, and NDC/lot/potency/expiration records are required.

Supply, purchasing/reporting and patient operations (notes only): access to all prescribed FDA-approved brands/assays/vial sizes, supplier lists and alternate pharmacy referral; incident reporting to prescriber/HTC within one business day; no outpatient billing for inpatient use; audit records and purchase invoices; recall notification system, notification within 24 hours when required/recommended, replacement prescription and retrieval/quarantine within seven days; counseling, no pharmacy-directed brand/dose selection or gifts, and required provider training/continuing education.

Appendices and forms (notes only): responsibility matrices, intake/treatment plan, pharmacokinetic monitoring, emergency stock, infusion logs, monthly/on-demand contacts and continuing education remain operational documentation. Remaining gaps: evidence verification, authorization/renewal/transfer, quantity logistics, all provider SOC operations, purchasing/reporting, forms and appendices require manual review.

Patient is in normal sinus rhythm.

Tried and failed OR has a contraindication to beta blockers at maximally tolerated dose.

Cautions (notes only): glucocorticoid dose should be maintained at or above the dose necessary for endogenous cortisol replacement; patients below this level are at increased risk of acute adrenal insufficiency or adrenal crisis. Quantity (notes only): 34 day supply at FDA approved dose.

Documentation, duration, quantity enforcement and cautions require manual review; this pack remains partial.

Andembry is linked as an HAE prophylaxis alternative and requires separate evaluation of its one-preferred-agent step. Dawnzera requires at least two preferred agents from two different therapeutic classes.

criteria.text: Source of calories and fatty acids for pediatric and adult patients with molecularly confirmed long-chain fatty acid oxidation disorders (LC-FAOD).

Molecularly confirmed LC-FAOD diagnosis based on at least TWO: (a) disease-specific elevations of acylcarnitines on a newborn blood spot or in plasma; (b) enzyme activity assay in cultured fibroblasts or lymphocytes below the reporting laboratory normal reference range; (c) genetic testing demonstrating a pathogenic mutation in a gene associated with LC-FAOD (approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with an endocrinologist or metabolic disease specialist (approval criterion 2).
Prescriber has submitted the patient's weight AND total prescribed daily caloric intake (approval criterion 3).
Dose does not exceed 35% of daily caloric intake (approval criterion 4).

Cautions (notes only): avoid co-administration of Pancreatic Lipase Inhibitors due to potential for reduced clinical effect.
Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization approval up to 12 months.

Bullous Pemphigoid: confirmed by serology or biopsy; BPDAI ≥24 and Peak Pruritus NRS ≥4; failed ≥2 standard therapies (different MOA) ≥1 month each; initially combined with tapering oral corticosteroids.
Denial if used in conjunction with another biologic medication (e.g. Enbrel, Xolair, Remicade).

The PDF parenthetical says "3 2mg vials", inconsistent with its 2 ml vial units; verify against labeling. HCPCS J9333. max_units is null because multiple windows and dosing require manual review.

Initial approval only. Nine closed diagnoses; all-request denials apply to all. SHOX does not cite Table 1. No invented numeric age or specialty gates. Path selects attest all constituent conditions; first-met ordering makes overlapping clinical branches mutually exclusive selections without changing eligibility.

Pediatric GHD approval nesting: growth failure + additional pituitary deficiencies OR growth failure + hypothalamic/pituitary surgery/irradiation OR ((velocity ≥2 SD below mean OR (height ≥2 SD below mean AND velocity >1 SD below mean)) AND (two subnormal stimulation tests OR one subnormal test + low IGF-1)). Open epiphyses and exclusion of other causes apply to every path.

SGA initial approval height wording (<2 SD below mean) is retained verbatim, not silently corrected. Reauthorization height wording and pediatric GHD/CKD height approval-versus-denial inconsistencies require manual source review.
Reauthorization SHOX, Noonan and Turner (notes only): approve pediatric patients not at final adult height or completed linear growth; deny at final adult height or completed linear growth.

Reauthorization Prader-Willi (notes only): BMI <35 kg/m², no severe respiratory impairment or untreated severe OSA, and not at final adult height/completed linear growth. Deny final height/completed growth, BMI ≥35, or severe respiratory impairment/untreated severe OSA.

Reauthorization CKD (notes only): no kidney transplant, previous GH ≤3 years, not attained mid-parental target height OR height not within 3rd percentile of normal adult height (65 inches boys/60 inches girls), and open epiphyses. Deny transplant, previous GH >3 years, attained mid-parental height OR height within that adult-height percentile, closed epiphyses, or final adult height/completed linear growth.

Reauthorization SGA (notes only): born SGA (birth weight or length ≥2 SD below gestational-age mean), height has not caught up to being <2 SD below age/gender mean, and pediatric patient not at final adult height/completed linear growth. Deny not born SGA, height caught up to <2 SD below mean, or final adult height/completed growth.

Reauthorization pediatric GHD (notes only): open epiphyses; pre-treatment growth rate doubled OR increased ≥3 cm/year in first treatment year OR growth rate ≥2.5 cm/year beyond first year; has not yet achieved mid-parental height OR height is within 3rd percentile normal adult height (65 inches boys/60 inches girls), as printed. Deny bone age =16 years males or =14 females, closed epiphyses, growth rate <2.5 cm/year past year, or whichever occurs sooner: reached mid-parental height OR height within 3rd percentile adult height. Mid-parental height = (father’s height + mother’s height)/2, plus 2.5 inches males or minus 2.5 inches females. Conflicting approval/denial height wording is not resolved into predicates.

Reauthorization transition and adult GHD (notes only): yearly clinical assessment evaluating adverse effects, IGF-1 and other GH-response parameters; assessment indicates response and continued need. Deny absent yearly assessment/evaluation, lack of response, or no continued need.
Initial coverage up to 6 months; reauthorization up to 12 months. Quantity limit: None. Duration and all reauthorization criteria require manual review.

FDA matrix and Table 1 are reference notes only, not hard product predicates. Zorbtive is FDA-labeled for short bowel syndrome but Alaska explicitly denies SBS; ISS is likewise denied despite some FDA labels. Skytrofa is lonapegsomatropin-tcgd within this class PDF. Alternatives empty: Serostim HIV wasting is outside this closed diagnosis list and is not an interchangeable covered indication.

Baseline score documentation and step therapy are attestations requiring chart verification. The antidepressant class attestation requires two distinct listed classes and ≥8 weeks each; augmentation requires ≥1 tried and failed therapy for ≥8 weeks. No numeric baseline score threshold is specified.
FDA usage (notes only): TRD in adults as monotherapy or with an oral antidepressant; MDD with acute suicidal ideation or behavior in adults in conjunction with an oral antidepressant.

Cautions (notes only): cardiovascular/cerebrovascular conditions and risk factors may increase adverse effects. May impair attention, judgment, thinking, reaction speed and motor skills; do not drive or operate machinery until the next day after restful sleep. May cause fetal harm; consider pregnancy planning and prevention in females of reproductive potential.
Duration (notes only): initial approval 3 months; reauthorization 12 months with chart notes showing improvement from the baseline depression score.

Quantity (notes only): 8 × 56mg dose kits/month or 8 × 84mg dose kits/month; maximum 84mg twice weekly. Physician administered claims HCPCS J0013 (max 84 HCPCS per treatment). Pharmacy Point-of-Sale payment as of October 2022. max_units is null; quantity is not evaluated.
Documentation verification, FDA usage, limitations, cautions, duration, reauthorization and quantity require manual review; this pack remains partial.

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Stelara (ustekinumab) for subcutaneous administration, Version 4. Original 11/14/2014; Revision Approval 9/20/2024; Effective 11/1/2024.
Approval #2 severity context: moderate to severe PsO, active PsA, moderate to severe active CD, and moderate to severely active UC are represented by the closed indication labels.
Specialty gap: the Alaska PDF specifies no prescriber specialty requirement; no specialty field or predicate is added.

All four indications require TNF blocker failure plus at least one other therapy; PsO includes at least one topical agent. Prior TNF failure is separate from prohibited concurrent integrin antagonist or TNF blocker use. No minimum trial duration is specified.

Disease activity uses categorical attestations, not numeric score coercion. PsO PASI ≥12 also covers denial #5 for initiators; PsA HAQ-DI ≥2; CD baseline CDAI and UC baseline Mayo (or equivalent) must be submitted.

Initial authorization (notes only): monitoring plan; previous therapies and nature of failure; current weight; complete medication regimen; confirmation not receiving concurrent phototherapy; dosing conforms to an FDA-approved regimen by indication. Documentation and dosing require manual review.

Reauthorization beyond 4 weeks (notes only): letter of medical necessity plus chart notes demonstrating therapeutic benefit: baseline/current PASI for Ps; tender/swollen joints, HAQ-DI (or equivalent), CRP for PsA; CDAI at baseline and at 6 months for CD (source reauthorization text spells CADI). Document tolerance and absence of adverse events.
Duration (notes only): initial 4 weeks (injections at 0 and 4 weeks); reauthorization up to 12 months (week 16 and beyond every 12 weeks). FDA regimen by indication requires manual review.

Manual review: 45 mg/dose for weight ≤100 kg; 90 mg/dose for weight >100 kg for plaque psoriasis; 90 mg/dose for CD and UC after initial IV infusion. Weight, route, and quantity limits are not numerically enforced.

Cautions (notes only): initial dose under physician supervision; subsequent self-administration only with physician determination, training and demonstrated competency, close monitoring and follow-up. Monitor new/worsening neurological issues for RPLS; no live vaccines unless benefit outweighs risk; avoid excessive UV exposure and monitor new skin growths; monitor therapeutic effect of CYP450 therapies, especially narrow therapeutic index agents. IL-12/IL-23 p40 binding may increase malignancy risk. Refer to prescribing information and medication guide.

PDL context: all STELARA vial, syringe and IV rows are non_preferred in CYTOKINE AND CAM ANTAGONISTS. Preferred peers without packs include Humira, Hadlima and Rinvoq (notes only). Infliximab has a separate partial class pack with product-specific PDL status in its notes. Linked alternatives require indication-specific review and do not imply confirmed coverage. Dupixent, Adbry and Ebglyss belong to IMMUNOMODULATORS, ATOPIC DERMATITIS and are not linked alternatives.
This pack remains partial: initial documentation, reauthorization, monitoring, cautions, duration, dosing and quantity enforcement require manual review.

Prescribed by or in consultation with a neurologist.
MGFA clinical classification II, III, or IV.
Positive anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody serology.
Baseline MG-ADL total score at least 6.
Documented inadequate response or labeled contraindication to qualifying immunosuppressive therapy.
Completed or current meningococcal vaccination for serogroups A, C, W, Y AND B at least 2 weeks before the first dose.
Prescriber enrolled in the REMS program.
No evidence of active meningococcal infection.

notes: Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid Zilbrysq (zilucoplan) Criteria Version 1; Original 12/21/2023; Accepted 01/19/2024; Effective 03/01/2024.

Approval criteria 1-7 and denial criteria 2-3 are encoded as attestations. AChR positivity is required; MuSK positivity alone does not qualify. Immunosuppressive examples include azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, cyclophosphamide, methotrexate, tacrolimus and rituximab. The chronic plasma exchange/plasmapheresis/IVIG pathway has no stated 12-month minimum.

Cautions (notes only): life-threatening and fatal meningococcal infections have occurred with complement inhibitors and may progress rapidly if not recognized and treated early. Pancreatitis and pancreatic cysts have been reported. Based on animal data, Zilbrysq may cause fetal harm.
Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization up to 12 months with prescriber documentation of positive clinical response and tolerability.
Quantity (manual review): 32.4 mg per day; 30 prefilled syringes per 30 days. max_units is null; dosing and quantity enforcement require manual review.
Rystiggo is an alternative for overlapping gMG eligibility; its own antibody and treatment-history criteria require separate review.
Remains partial: evidence documentation, cautions, duration, reauthorization, dosing and quantity require manual review. PDL status unknown.

criteria.text: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) with bi-allelic SMN1 mutations (FDA indication; approval 3).
Patient is less than 2 years old (approval 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a pediatric neurologist (approval 2).
SMN1 mutation confirmed by genetic testing (approval 4).
Anti-AAV9 antibody titer ≤ 1:50 (approval 5).
No concomitant SMA modifying therapy (approval 6).
Baseline LFT, platelet count and Troponin-I conducted within 30 days of request, each < 2× ULN (approval 7).
Not previously treated with Zolgensma (denial 2).
SMA is not advanced, e.g. complete limb paralysis, permanent ventilator dependence or tracheostomy (denial 3).
No active, unresolved infection (denial 4).

notes: Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid Zolgensma (onasemnogene abeparvovec-xioi), an AAV vector gene therapy. Version: 1; Original: 08/2/2023; Accepted: 09/15/2023; Effective: 11/1/2023.
Encoded: closed SMA indication, approval criteria 1–7 and denial criteria 2–4. Denial 1 is failure to meet approval criteria. Genetic confirmation is a separate attestation.
No concomitant SMA modifying therapy, e.g. nusinersen or risdiplam.
Duration (notes only): initial approval 3 months; no reauthorization will be approved.
Quantity (notes only): one infusion per lifetime; total dose not to exceed 1.1×10^14 vector genomes (vg) per kg. HCPCS J3590.

Limitations of use: safety and effectiveness of repeat administration have not been evaluated. Use in advanced SMA (e.g. complete paralysis of limbs, permanent ventilator dependence) has not been evaluated.

Cautions (notes only): if liver function abnormalities persist ≥ 2 times ULN after the 30-day period of systemic corticosteroids, promptly consult a pediatric gastroenterologist or hepatologist. Acute liver failure has been reported; preexisting hepatic impairment may increase risk.

Documentation and numeric laboratory results require manual review; baseline testing, timing and thresholds are encoded as a combined attestation. Duration, no reauthorization, lifetime quantity, dose and cautions remain notes only, so this pack remains partial.
PDL status remains unknown. Evrysdi / Spinraza is a separately evaluated SMA alternative; that pack excludes prior SMA gene replacement therapy.

criteria.text: Diagnosis of seizures associated with CDKL5 deficiency disorder (CDD) (approval criterion 3).
Patient is 2 years of age or older (approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a neurologist (approval criterion 2).
Patient has a genetically confirmed mutation in the CDKL5 gene which is pathogenic or likely pathogenic (approval criterion 4).
Patient has tried and failed or is currently taking at least two previous antiepileptic drugs (approval criterion 5).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Ztalmy (ganaxolone) Criteria. Version 1; Original 2/28/2023; Accepted 4/21/2023; Effective 6/1/2023.

Encoded: approval criteria 1–5 for the single closed CDD seizures indication. Failure to meet approval criteria is a denial. Neurologist consultation, genetic confirmation and prior/current antiepileptic therapy are attestations requiring documentation verification.

Genetic confirmation requires a pathogenic or likely pathogenic CDKL5 mutation; a variant of uncertain significance does not qualify. Prior therapy requires tried and failed OR currently taking at least two previous antiepileptic drugs. No specific drugs or minimum trial duration are specified; contraindication alone does not satisfy this criterion.

Cautions (notes only): ganaxolone is a schedule V (C-V) controlled substance. Monitor for suicidal behavior and ideation. Withdraw gradually to minimize increased seizure frequency or status epilepticus. Ztalmy may cause fetal harm.
Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization up to 6 months with confirmation of a sustained reduction in monthly seizure frequency from pre-treatment baseline.
Quantity (notes only): 1800 mg (36 ml) daily. max_units is null; dosing and quantity are not evaluated.
Documentation verification, cautions, duration, reauthorization, dosing and quantity enforcement require manual review; this pack remains partial.

criteria.text: Diagnosis of postpartum depression (PPD).
Adult age: at least 18 years.
Prescribed by or in consultation with a psychiatrist.
Major depressive episode began no earlier than the third trimester of pregnancy and no later than 4 weeks following delivery.
No more than 12 months have elapsed since delivery (12 months included).

Tried and failed an agent at a recognized therapeutic dose for at least 6 weeks from at least one of: SSRI, SNRI, bupropion, mirtazapine, TCA; OR has a contraindication to ALL five listed classes/agents.
Current laboratory assessments, including BOTH renal and liver function tests, within the last 60 days.
eGFR is at least 15 mL/min/1.73 m² (15 included; below 15 is denied).
Prior treatment with Zulresso or Zurzuvae for the current pregnancy.

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Zurzuvae Criteria Version 1; Original: 12/18/2023; Accepted: 01/19/2024; Effective: 03/01/2024. Archived source and effective date retained.

Encoded: closed postpartum_depression indication, adult age ≥18, psychiatrist prescribing or consultation, major depressive episode onset from the third trimester through 4 weeks after delivery inclusive, ≤12 months since delivery, ≥6 weeks at therapeutic dose of one listed antidepressant or contraindication to all listed classes/agents, and current renal and liver labs within 60 days. Clinical requirements are attestations; verify supporting documentation. Failure to meet approval criteria is represented by approval predicates.

Denials encoded: eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m² (eGFR ≥15 qualifies by attestation); prior Zulresso or Zurzuvae treatment for the current pregnancy. Treatment for an earlier pregnancy alone is not this exclusion.
Duration (notes only): initial approval 1 month; treatment limited to 14 days; no extension of therapy will be authorized.
Quantity (notes only): #28 for 14 days; one course of treatment per pregnancy. Duration and quantity enforcement require manual review.

Cautions (notes only): avoid CYP3A4 inducers; the source PDF says CYP4A4 inducers (apparent typo). CNS depression and impaired driving: no driving or other potentially hazardous activities until at least 12 hours after administration. Abuse potential with risks of misuse, abuse, substance abuse disorder and addiction. May cause fetal harm. Cautions require manual review and are not additional denial predicates.

criteria.text: Adult maintenance treatment of moderately to severely active UC or CD following IV infliximab (FDA indications; approval #3).
Patient is 18 years or older (FDA labeled age; approval #1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a gastroenterologist (approval #2).
Received IV infliximab for ≥10 weeks and demonstrated a positive clinical response (approval #4).
Patient is not and will not be on concurrent treatment with another biologic agent (e.g. TNF-inhibitory, interleukin inhibitor, biologic response modifier; approval #5).
Evaluated and screened for latent tuberculosis and hepatitis B virus infection prior to initiating treatment (approval #6).
No clinically significant infection (denial #2).
No history of malignancy (denial #3).
No history of moderate to severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) (denial #4).
No history of congestive heart failure (CHF) (denial #5).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Zymfentra Criteria Version 1: Original 03/12/2025; Accepted 04/18/2025; Effective 06/01/2025.

Zymfentra is a TNF blocker for SC maintenance after IV infliximab. Both adult UC and CD indications share all encoded criteria. Diagnosis severity is covered by the closed indication labels. Denial #1 is failure to meet approval criteria.
Duration (notes only): authorization up to 12 months. The PDF does not specify a separate initial/reauthorization split.
Quantity and dosing (manual review): 2 prefilled pens or syringes every 28 days; maximum dose 120 mg every 14 days (120 mg q14d ceiling). Quantity metadata does not numerically enforce these limits.

Cautions (notes only): increased malignancy risk, including lymphoma; monitor hepatic enzymes and liver function tests every 3 to 4 months due to severe hepatic reaction risk; increased severe infection risk; avoid live vaccines during treatment.

PDL context: Zymfentra is non_preferred. Preferred cytokine peers without rule packs (e.g. Humira, Hadlima, Rinvoq) are notes only. Linked alternatives require their own criteria review. IV Infliximab is a separate partial peer with its own criteria.
This pack remains partial: duration, dosing, quantity enforcement, monitoring and cautions require manual review.

criteria.text: Adult and pediatric patients with β-thalassemia who require regular red blood cell (RBC) transfusions (FDA indication; approval criterion 3).
Patient is 4 years of age or older (approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a hematologist (approval criterion 2).
Diagnosis of β-thalassemia confirmed by genetic testing (approval criterion 3).
Patient weighs a minimum of 6 kg (approval criterion 4).
Able to provide adequate cells to meet the minimum recommended dose of 5.0×10^6 CD34+ cells/kg (approval criterion 5).
Negative tests for HBV, HCV, HIV, and HTLV-1&2 prior to collection of cells (approval criterion 6).
Documented history of ≥100 mL/kg/year of pRBCs in the immediately preceding two years OR ≥8 transfusions of pRBCs in the immediately preceding two years (approval criterion 7).
No previous gene therapy for transfusion-dependent thalassemia (TDT) (denial criterion 2).
No previous allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) for TDT (denial criterion 3).

notes: Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid Zynteglo (betibeglogene autotemcel), autologous hematopoietic stem cell-based gene therapy for transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia. Version: 1; Original: 10/9/2024; Accepted: 11/15/2024; Effective: 01/01/2025. The PDF heading spells the generic betibeglogene-autoemcel.
Encoded: FDA indication, approval criteria 1-7 and denial exclusions 2-3. Denial criterion 1 (failure to meet approval criteria) is covered by the approval clauses.
Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 6 months; no reauthorization will be approved.
Quantity (notes only): one infusion per lifetime; HCPCS J3393. No numeric quantity enforcement; max_units is null.

Cautions (notes only): monitor platelet and neutrophil counts following infusion due to delayed or failed engraftment risk. Monitor for hematologic malignancy at least annually for a minimum of 15 years following infusion.

Cautions (notes only): avoid antiretroviral medications or hydroxyurea beginning a minimum of one month, or for the expected duration of elimination of all such medications, prior to mobilization until all cycles of apheresis are completed.

Cautions (notes only): discontinue iron chelators seven days before myeloablative conditioning and avoid until six months after Zynteglo infusion. Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) may cause hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis.

Remaining gaps: documentation verification, duration, no reauthorization, lifetime quantity enforcement and monitoring require manual review. Genetic confirmation, adequate CD34+ cell dose, infectious testing and transfusion history are attestations.
PDL status unknown. No evaluate-linked alternatives.
